case_title: Chinnam Kameswara Rao and Ors. v. State of A.P.
aggravating_circumstances: Premeditated plan, threat of dire consequences, use of weapons, fatal injuries
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302 IPC and causing grievous hurt under s.324 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, along with another individual, confronted the deceased and an injured witness. The accused were armed with sticks and assaulted the deceased and the injured witness, causing grievous injuries. The deceased later succumbed to his injuries. The incident was a sequel to a previous altercation between the accused and the deceased and the injured witness. The accused were charged with causing death and causing injuries. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court reversed the acquittal and convicted the accused for murder and causing grievous hurt. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence to establish the guilt of the accused.
